title: Establishing Human Lung Organoids and Proximal Differentiation to Generate Mature Airway Organoids.
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for culture of human airway organoids from adult stem cells

### Overview

This protocol details the derivation, expansion, passaging, and differentiation of human airway organoids from adult stem cells isolated from freshly resected human lung tissue. The process involves enzymatic digestion of lung tissue to isolate stem cells, embedding in basement matrix for 3D organoid formation, mechanical or enzymatic passaging, and subsequent differentiation into either 3D proximal airway organoids or 2D airway epithelium on permeable supports for downstream analysis.

### Materials/Reagents

Advanced DMEM/F12 medium, Glutamine (2 mM), HEPES (10 mM), Penicillin (100 U/mL), Streptomycin (100 µg/mL), R-spondin 1 conditioned medium (10%), Noggin conditioned medium (10%), B27 supplement (1x), N-acetylcysteine (1.25 mM), Nicotinamide (10 mM), Y-27632 (5 µM for expansion; 10 µM for differentiation), A-83-01 (500 nM), SB202190 (1 µM), Fibroblast growth factor (FGF)-7 (5 ng/mL), FGF-10 (20 ng/mL), Primocin (100 µg/mL), Heregulin beta-1 (5 nM), Air liquid interface basal medium, Air liquid interface supplement (1x), Air liquid interface maintenance supplement (1x), Heparin (4 µg/mL), Hydrocortisone (1 µM), DAPT (10 µM), Collagenase (2 mg/mL final concentration), Fetal bovine serum (FBS) (2% for digestion termination; 40 µL for passaging), Red blood cell lysis buffer, Basement matrix, Dissociation enzyme (e.g., Trypsin), EDTA (10 mM), Cell lysate buffer.

### Equipment

Biosafety hood, Sterile scalpel, 10 cm cell culture dish, 15 mL centrifuge tubes, Centrifuge (capable of 400 x g at 4 °C and 300 x g at 4 °C), Shaker/incubator (capable of 120 rpm at 37 °C), 10 mL serological pipette, 100 µm strainer, 50 mL centrifuge tubes, 40 µm strainer, Cell counter, 24-well suspension culture plate, 24-well permeable support inserts, 12-well permeable support inserts, Pasteur pipettes (standard and narrowed tip), Bunsen burner, Autoclave, 37 °C water bath, Microscope (with 4x magnification capability).

### Safety & Sterility

All procedures involving human tissue must be performed inside a biosafety hood. Maintain sterile conditions throughout tissue processing, cell isolation, and culture steps. Use cold media and keep samples on ice during basement matrix handling to prevent premature solidification. Ensure proper sterilization of glassware (e.g., autoclaving modified Pasteur pipettes).

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare basal medium by supplementing advanced DMEM/F12 medium with 2 mM glutamine, 10 mM HEPES, 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 µg/mL streptomycin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare human lung organoid expansion medium by supplementing the prepared basal medium with 10% R-spondin 1 conditioned medium, 10% Noggin conditioned medium, 1x B27 supplement, 1.25 mM N-acetylcysteine, 10 mM nicotinamide, 5 µM Y-27632, 500 nM A-83-01, 1 µM SB202190, 5 ng/mL fibroblast growth factor (FGF)-7, 20 ng/mL FGF-10, and 100 µg/mL primocin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare proximal differentiation medium (PD medium) by supplementing air liquid interface basal medium with 1x air liquid interface supplement, 1x air liquid interface maintenance supplement, 4 µg/mL heparin, 1 µM hydrocortisone, 10 µM Y-27632, and 10 µM DAPT. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Cell Isolation and 3D Organoid Derivation

### Day 0: Tissue Procurement and Processing

1. Procure freshly resected human lung tissues (approximately 0.5 cm in size) from patients undergoing surgical resection. Transport the tissues in 30 mL of basal medium at room temperature and process them as quickly as possible inside a biosafety hood. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Mince the lung tissues into small pieces (0.5–1 mm) using a sterile scalpel within a 10 cm cell culture dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Wash the tissue pieces with 10 mL of cold basal medium in a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Resuspend the pellet in 8 mL of basal medium supplemented with collagenase to a final concentration of 2 mg/mL. Digest the tissue pieces by shaking the tube at 120 rpm for 30–40 min at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Pipet up and down 20 times using a 10 mL serological pipette to shear the digested tissue pieces. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Stack a 100 µm strainer on a 50 mL centrifuge tube and filter the suspension through it. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. Transfer the filtered suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Perform a second round of shearing after filtering. Additional shearing-filtering cycles (1–2 times) may be performed to isolate more cells, particularly if the initial tissue piece was small (<0.5 cm). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
8. Add fetal bovine serum (FBS) to the flow-through to a final concentration of 2% to terminate digestion. Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
9. Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of basal medium. Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->

#### Branch: Optional RBC Lysis

1. (Optional) If erythrocytes are visible in the pellet, resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of red blood cell lysis buffer and incubate at room temperature for 5 min. Add 10 mL of basal medium, centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at 4 °C, and discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Resuspend the final cell pellet in cold basement matrix and keep on ice. Use 80–160 µL of basement matrix for cells recovered from ~0.5 cm of lung tissue, which is sufficient to seed 2–4 droplets. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->

### Day 0: Embedding

1. Prewarm a 24-well suspension culture plate in a cell culture incubator set to 37 °C with 5% CO2 and a humidified atmosphere. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Dispense 40 µL of the cell-basement matrix suspension into each well of the prewarmed 24-well suspension culture plate. Incubate at 37 °C for 10–15 min to allow the basement matrix to solidify into droplets. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Add 500 µL of human lung organoid expansion medium supplemented with 5 nM Heregulin beta-1 to each well. Incubate the plate in the cell culture incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->

### Expansion Phase

1. Refresh the medium every 3 days. Carefully remove the old medium while keeping the droplet intact and add fresh medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Passage the organoids after an incubation period of 10–14 days. Note that Heregulin beta-1 should only be used in the initial culture before the first passage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
3. Observe the organoids under a microscope to ensure they are not embedded at excessively high cell density. If a droplet disintegrates due to high cell density, recover the organoids and cells, re-embed them in a higher volume of basement matrix to create more droplets with lower, desirable cell densities. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->

## Organoid Passaging

### Passaging Event

1. Harvest the lung organoids as described in the initial tissue processing steps (Section 2.2.1 equivalent: digest, filter, and collect cells). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->

#### Branch: Mechanical Shearing

1. Use a 1 mL pipette tip to pipet up and down to break the droplets. Transfer the organoids and medium to a 15 mL centrifuge tube and adjust the volume to 10 mL with cold basal medium. Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant. Wash the organoids once again with 10 mL of cold basal medium. Resuspend the organoids in 2 mL of cold basal medium. Shear the organoids into small pieces using a Pasteur pipette. Check the size of the organoid pieces under a microscope at 4x magnification. Add 40 µL of FBS to terminate any residual digestion. NOTE: Determine fragment size based on experimental needs. For more uniform or smaller fragments (or single cells), shear further; this may extend the time to readiness to approximately 3 weeks. Supplement with basal medium to a total volume of 10 mL, centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C, and resuspend the fragments in cold basement matrix sufficient for a 1:3 to 1:5 expansion ratio. Keep on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->

#### Branch: Trypsinization

1. (Alternative: Trypsinization) Use this method if mechanical shearing is difficult, organoid size is highly variable, or uniform size is required. Prepare a Pasteur pipette by narrowing its tip from 1.5 mm to ~1.0 mm using a flame, cool it, and autoclave it. Wet the pipette with basal medium to prevent cell attachment. Resuspend organoids in 1 mL of dissociation enzyme and incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 3–5 min. Add 1 mL of basal medium. Shear mechanically using the modified Pasteur pipette. Check size under a microscope at 4x magnification. Add 40 µL of FBS to terminate digestion. Filter through a 40 µm strainer into a 50 mL centrifuge tube, then transfer to a 15 mL tube. Top up with basal medium to 10 mL total volume, centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C. Resuspend the pellet (from 24 droplets of 40 µL each) in 1–2.5 mL of lung organoid expansion medium depending on cell density. Count cells using a microscope cell counter. Adjust concentration to 1.3 x 10^6/mL for 24-well inserts or 9 x 10^5/mL for 12-well inserts. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Resuspend organoid pieces in cold basement matrix with a volume sufficient for a 1:5 to 1:10 passage ratio. Keep on ice. Place 40 µL of suspension in each well of a prewarmed 24-well plate. Incubate at 37 °C for 10–15 min to solidify. Supplement with 500 µL of lung organoid expansion medium per well and incubate. Refresh medium every 3 days. Passage organoids after 2–3 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->

## Differentiation into Airway Organoids

### Differentiation Start

1. Prepare sufficient 3D lung organoids for 2D airway differentiation. Seed 1.3 x 10^5 cells for a 24-well permeable support insert or 4.5 x 10^5 cells for a 12-well permeable support insert. Pre-incubate inserts with basal medium overnight in the incubator. Add 250 µL basal medium to the top chamber and 500 µL to the bottom chamber for 24-well plates; for 12-well plates, add 500 µL to the top and 1,000 µL to the bottom. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->

#### Branch: 3D Airway Organoids

1. Harvest 3D lung organoids as described in step 1. Incubate lung organoids in the expansion medium for 7-10 days after passaging via mechanical shearing. Replace the expansion medium with the PD medium. Incubate the organoids in the PD medium for 14 days in a cell culture incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->

#### Branch: 2D Airway Organoids

1. (For 2D Airway Organoids) After growing 3D organoids in expansion medium for 2 weeks, digest them into single cells. Remove basal medium from the top and bottom chambers of the inserts. Add 500 µL expansion medium to the bottom chamber of the 24-well insert and 1,000 µL to the 12-well insert. Seed 100 µL of cell suspension onto the apical chamber of the 24-well insert and 500 µL onto the 12-well insert. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
2. (For 2D Airway Organoids) Incubate for 2 days. Replace the expansion medium with PD medium in both the apical and bottom chambers. Incubate for 14 days, refreshing the PD medium every 3 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->

#### Branch: Harvest for Analysis

1. (Harvest for Analysis) Discard the PD medium. Add cell lysate buffer to harvest differentiated airway organoids for RNA extraction and RT-qPCR gene expression analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->

#### Branch: Flow Cytometry Prep

1. (Flow Cytometry Prep) Alternatively, add 10 mM EDTA and incubate organoids at 37 °C for 60 min to dissociate them into single cells. Proceed with flow cytometry analysis to examine cell populations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
